provenance: OC-020: synthetic graded-pack case exercising coupled-search schema v10 per-region tape-spec assignment. Racetrack skeleton matches the OC-007 family (0.3 m straight half-length, 0.2 m bend radius); the two grading regions split turns_along_normal at the radial midpoint: inner half (higher field) may take the base tape or the low-field-binned variant, outer half (lower field) the same pair. Both specs bind real embedded measured datasets -- base is robinson-superpower-ap-v3 (csv_sha256 889cc2cf8b91b822cbc6cceb7388e5d8afcb8a8911bb20ab175e50c7e6dc0354), 'hts-lowfield' is robinson-superpower-ap-v3-lowfield (csv_sha256 043cbaab9a32da5de6394b136265835b9c5917e28861d0793544c5e3885f893b) -- so the mechanism under test is honest per-region material resolution, not an invented conductor. Prices (base 30 USD/m, hts-lowfield 18 USD/m, plus the OC-007 placeholder assembly/joint/scrap figures) are invented placeholders, not supplier data; the result is a modeled saving under a screening model, never a production claim. Schema v10 forbids the `refinement` block on graded cases (assignment-aware bisection is not implemented), so none is declared; the baseline assignment is all-base at the cheapest all-base feasible geometry (160x4), so savings read as grading-on-top-of-geometry. Note: the lowfield dataset shares the base dataset's measured rows in the field range this case operates in, so the two specs screen identically here and grading exercises per-region pricing and resolution rather than feasibility discrimination; that discrimination is covered by a declared-synthetic scaled-Ic unit test. Not a production design.
